speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what is the total amount of Government subsidies, grants and other financial support provided to Ubisoft Singapore from 2008 to 2024; (b) what specific key performance indicators and conditions are attached to the support provided in terms of local talent development, leadership roles for Singaporeans, and knowledge transfer; and (c) what mechanisms exist to claw back subsidies if companies fail to meet these conditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The level of support and conditions vary depending on the nature of the project.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: What key performance indicators (KPIs) and conditions were attached to support in terms of local talent development, leadership roles for Singaporeans and knowledge transfer?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And what are the mechanisms that he mentioned that the Government has to be able to claw back government funding if companies do not fulfil these obligations?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And has the Economic Development Board (EDB) ever clawed back public funding given to foreign companies who do not fulfil their obligations?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: With regard to Ubisoft and the broader games sector, those are applied, but the Government has been supporting and, indeed, growing this ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: With regards primarily to the question about building up local talent in this space, I thought it is useful to share a few nuggets.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: There are local leaders who have been developed, and I have met a few of them.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Paul Foo is a creative director who has been working at Ubisoft for many, many years.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The local team of Ubisoft Singapore and local developers have been working on the games in two regions, as the game is featured in Japan in the samurai era.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Broader to that, recently I was also at Koei Tecmo Singapore's 20th anniversary.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: They launched Three Kingdoms HEROES, which is on Apple Arcade, and they also worked together with our local Institutes of Higher Learning, for example, with Nanyang Polytechnic.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, I met with some of the developers who are doing a diploma in animation games and visual effects.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: There are two, for example, Goh Jia Hui and Lu Shi Ya, have been working on these games that these studios have been developing and are based in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, I think, overall, we support this ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We have also seen the good flow-down impact on creating very new and exciting jobs on the game developer space and we will continue to do so.
